concepts.name: Matter is composed of particles and can be classified according to composition and properties
learning_points: Classify matter into elements, compounds and mixtures

concepts.name: Chemical reactions follow quantitative laws governing the combination of substances
learning_points: State law of conservation of mass
Understand reciprocal proportions at the required level
Apply laws to simple chemical problems

concepts.name: Relative atomic and molecular masses compare particle masses with a standard reference
learning_points: Use relative atomic masses in chemical calculations

concepts.name: The mole is the SI unit for amount of substance and represents a fixed number of specified entities
learning_points: Convert between number of particles and moles

concepts.name: The mass percentage of each element can be determined from the composition of a compound
learning_points: Use atomic masses in composition calculations

concepts.name: Elemental composition can be used to determine empirical and molecular formulae
learning_points: Determine molecular formula using molar mass

concepts.name: Stoichiometry quantitatively relates reactants and products in a chemical reaction
Atoms contain smaller subatomic particles with characteristic masses and charges
learning_points: Compare charge and mass of subatomic particles

concepts.name: Early atomic models attempted to explain the structure and distribution of charge inside atoms
Bohr proposed that electrons occupy quantised stationary orbits with discrete energies
learning_points: Explain hydrogen spectrum using Bohr model

concepts.name: Electromagnetic radiation exhibits wave properties characterised by wavelength, frequency and speed
Energy exchange between matter and radiation occurs in discrete quanta
learning_points: Relate photon energy to frequency and wavelength

concepts.name: Moving particles possess wave-like characteristics
Quantum mechanics describes electrons using wavefunctions and probability distributions rather than fixed classical orbits
Quantum numbers specify allowed states and characteristics of electrons in atoms
learning_points: Relate quantum numbers to shells and subshells

concepts.name: Electrons occupy orbitals according to energy ordering and quantum-mechanical principles
learning_points: Understand stability of half-filled and completely filled subshells

chapters.title: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

concepts.name: Elements can be systematically classified according to recurring patterns in their properties
learning_points: Recognise achievements and limitations of Mendeleev classification

concepts.name: Properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers
learning_points: Understand blocks of the periodic table
Relate electronic configuration to periodic position

concepts.name: Atomic and ionic radii vary systematically across periods and down groups
Ionisation enthalpy reflects the energy required to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom
Electron gain enthalpy describes energy change associated with adding an electron to a gaseous atom
Electronegativity measures the tendency of an atom to attract shared electrons in a chemical bond
Valency and chemical behaviour show periodic relationships with electronic configuration
learning_points: Understand periodic variation in metallic character

concepts.name: Atoms tend toward stable valence-shell configurations through electron transfer or sharing
Ionic bonding arises from electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions
learning_points: Explain formation of cations and anions
Relate ionic size to lattice properties

concepts.name: Covalent bonds form through sharing of electron pairs between atoms
Chemical bonds have measurable structural and energetic characteristics
learning_points: Relate bond order to length and strength

concepts.name: Electron pairs around a central atom arrange themselves to minimise repulsions
Covalent bonds can be described as overlap of atomic orbitals
learning_points: Relate hybrid orbitals to molecular geometry
Understand limitations of simple valence-bond description

concepts.name: Hybridisation combines atomic orbitals to form equivalent hybrid orbitals suited to molecular geometry
Atomic orbitals combine to form molecular orbitals spread over the molecule
learning_points: Understand sigma and pi molecular orbitals
Predict magnetic behaviour at the required level

concepts.name: Hydrogen bonding is a strong directional intermolecular or intramolecular attraction involving hydrogen attached to highly electronegative atoms
learning_points: Distinguish intermolecular and intramolecular hydrogen bonding

concepts.name: A thermodynamic system is the portion of the universe selected for study and everything else constitutes its surroundings
learning_points: Distinguish open, closed and isolated systems

concepts.name: State functions depend only on the state of a system while path functions depend on the process followed
learning_points: Identify internal energy as a state function
Understand heat and work as path functions

concepts.name: Internal energy is the total microscopic energy contained within a system
learning_points: Relate internal energy to heat and work

concepts.name: Energy is conserved during chemical and physical processes
Enthalpy is a state function useful for describing heat changes at constant pressure
Chemical reactions involve measurable enthalpy changes that can be related to standard thermochemical quantities
The total enthalpy change of a reaction is independent of the pathway
Entropy measures dispersal of energy and is central to predicting the spontaneity of processes
learning_points: Relate entropy to disorder at the required level

concepts.name: Gibbs energy change combines enthalpy and entropy effects to provide a criterion for spontaneity at constant temperature and pressure
learning_points: Relate sign of ΔG to spontaneity

concepts.name: At equilibrium, forward and reverse reaction rates become equal while concentrations remain constant
For a reaction at equilibrium, the ratio of product and reactant activities follows a constant relationship at fixed temperature
An equilibrium system responds to imposed changes in concentration, pressure or temperature in a direction that tends to oppose the change
learning_points: Understand effect of catalysts on equilibrium

concepts.name: Electrolytes produce ions in solution and may undergo complete or partial ionisation
Acid-base behaviour can be described using Arrhenius, Bronsted-Lowry and Lewis frameworks
Water undergoes slight self-ionisation establishing a temperature-dependent ionic equilibrium
Buffer solutions resist significant changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added
learning_points: Apply Henderson-Hasselbalch relation at the required level

concepts.name: Sparingly soluble ionic compounds establish equilibria described by their solubility products
Oxidation and reduction can be described using oxygen/hydrogen transfer, electron transfer and oxidation-number changes
learning_points: Relate oxidation and reduction to oxidation number

concepts.name: Oxidation number is a bookkeeping quantity used to track electron redistribution in compounds and ions
learning_points: Calculate oxidation numbers in polyatomic ions

concepts.name: Redox equations can be balanced by conserving atoms and charge
learning_points: Balance redox reactions by oxidation-number method
Balance redox reactions by ion-electron method

concepts.name: Electron transfer reactions can be used for quantitative determination of substances

chapters.title: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

concepts.name: Carbon forms a vast variety of compounds because of its tetravalency and ability to catenate
learning_points: Recognise structural diversity of carbon compounds

concepts.name: Organic compounds can be classified according to carbon skeleton and functional groups
IUPAC rules provide a systematic method for naming organic compounds
learning_points: Apply priority rules at the required level

concepts.name: Isomers have the same molecular formula but differ in connectivity or spatial arrangement
learning_points: Understand stereoisomerism at the required level

concepts.name: Organic reactions involve characteristic patterns of bond breaking, bond formation and electron movement
Electron distribution within organic molecules influences their stability, reactivity and properties
learning_points: Understand hyperconjugation at the required level
Relate electronic effects to stability and reactivity

concepts.name: Organic compounds can be purified using physical methods based on differences in properties
Organic compounds can be analysed for constituent elements using characteristic chemical tests
learning_points: Understand basic principles of qualitative analysis

concepts.name: Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen and are classified according to bonding and structure
learning_points: Relate structure to degree of unsaturation

concepts.name: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons containing carbon-carbon single bonds
Alkenes contain carbon-carbon double bonds and undergo characteristic addition reactions
learning_points: Understand peroxide effect at the required level

concepts.name: Alkynes contain carbon-carbon triple bonds and exhibit addition and characteristic terminal-alkyne reactions
learning_points: Understand acidic character of terminal alkynes

concepts.name: Benzene is a planar aromatic system stabilised by delocalised pi electrons
learning_points: Understand Friedel-Crafts reactions at the required level

concepts.name: Hydrocarbon combustion and some hydrocarbon compounds can affect air quality and human health
learning_points: Recognise harmful effects of selected hydrocarbons

chapters.title: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

concepts.name: Organic molecules can be represented using molecular, structural, condensed and skeletal formulae
learning_points: Interpret skeletal representations at the required level

concepts.name: Functional groups determine characteristic chemical behaviour of organic molecules
learning_points: Relate functional groups to chemical properties

concepts.name: Short-lived reactive intermediates influence mechanisms and product formation
Organic reactions can be classified according to how bonds are broken and formed
Physical properties of substances depend strongly on interactions between their constituent particles
learning_points: Relate intermolecular forces to physical properties

concepts.name: Ideal gases approximately obey simple quantitative relationships among pressure, volume and temperature
The ideal gas equation combines the basic gas laws into a single relationship
learning_points: Apply equation to mixtures at the required level

concepts.name: In an ideal gas mixture, total pressure is the sum of partial pressures of individual gases
learning_points: Relate mole fraction to partial pressure

concepts.name: Gas behaviour can be explained by random motion and collisions of particles
Real gases deviate from ideal behaviour because particles have volume and intermolecular attractions
Liquids have characteristic properties arising from intermolecular interactions and molecular mobility
learning_points: Relate liquid properties to intermolecular forces

concepts.name: Solids can be classified according to the order and arrangement of their constituent particles
A crystal lattice is generated by regular repetition of a basic structural unit
learning_points: Identify primitive and centred unit cells

concepts.name: Particles can arrange themselves in efficient close-packed structures
Crystal density can be calculated from unit-cell dimensions and the number of particles per unit cell
learning_points: Calculate number of particles per unit cell
Relate edge length to atomic radius

concepts.name: Imperfections in crystal lattices influence physical and electrical properties
learning_points: Relate defects to density and properties

concepts.name: The electronic structure and lattice arrangement of solids determine their electrical and magnetic behaviour
learning_points: Classify magnetic behaviour at the required level
